_doc: How much thread a screw needs in the part it screws into, in multiples of the screw's major diameter, by what the part is made of: m3.major_diameter * engagement.plastic. Rules of thumb for a joint as strong as a class 8.8 screw: a calculation (VDI 2230) or a test decides a joint that matters. kind as in x1c.json.
name: engagement

steel.rule: Thread engaged in a tapped hole in steel, in screw diameters: about 1. Bossard gives 1.0 for a class 8.8 screw in S235 mild steel and 0.8 in hardened steel
steel.source: Nord-Lock, Thread engagement in a tapped hole, https://www.nord-lock.com/insights/bolting-tips/2015/the-experts-thread-engagement-in-a-tapped-hole/; Bossard, Length of engaged thread (01-2025), https://www.bossard.com/ie-en/knowledge-hub/resources/technical-information/length-of-engaged-thread/

aluminium.rule: Thread engaged in a tapped hole in aluminium, in screw diameters: about 2. Bossard gives 2 for a class 8.8 screw in soft AlMg3 and 1.4 in the stronger AlMgSi1 (6082)
aluminium.source: Nord-Lock, Thread engagement in a tapped hole, https://www.nord-lock.com/insights/bolting-tips/2015/the-experts-thread-engagement-in-a-tapped-hole/; Bossard, Length of engaged thread (01-2025), https://www.bossard.com/ie-en/knowledge-hub/resources/technical-information/length-of-engaged-thread/

plastic.rule: Thread engaged in printed plastic, in screw diameters, for a joint that carries load: 2 to 2.5 as Bambu Lab gives it, the upper figure here. 1.5 to 2 does where the joint holds no weight, and a thread-forming screw's maker asks 2 in ABS
plastic.source: Bambu Lab (MakerWorld official account), How to design screw holes for 3D printing, https://forum.bambulab.com/t/how-to-design-screw-holes-for-3d-printing/217352; PSM International, PT series screws, design recommendation, https://psmfasteners.com/product_guide/direct-screw-fixings-for-plastics-light-alloys-guide/pt-series/
